headline: Reanalysis of public single-cell data maps disease-linked cell states across tissues
label: Single Cell Lineage Profiling
summary: Donor-aware and cross-condition reanalysis of public single-cell datasets is extracting disease-associated cell states across tissues.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell transcriptomics applied to tissue-level disease questions, largely through reanalysis of public datasets. Several items integrate multiple cohorts or species: a six-dataset meta-analysis maps a ciliary gene panel onto TOF snRNA-seq, a multi-scale atlas spans 55,342 cardiomyocytes from human and mouse infarcted hearts, and a cross-species atlas covers 501,940 skeletal muscle cells across 2863 condition-time-state combinations. Donor-aware designs recur in the organoid and meniscus analyses, and the knee osteoarthritis reanalysis nominates stress and ferroptosis-associated programs as candidate mechanisms, not causal ones. Lineage-commitment and identity questions appear in the HGPS adipogenic study and the infarcted cardiomyocyte atlas, which describes identity erosion without proliferative re-entry. Methodological work benchmarks 11 cell segmentation methods across 15 spatial transcriptomics datasets. The common element is state-resolved readout used to prioritize, not establish, disease-linked programs.
